title: Workspace-wide canonical-template sweep: supports_type<O>(&self) → supports_type<O>(&self, caller, account_id)
description:
The 8 extension-server Backend traits (MailBackend, ChatBackend, CalendarsBackend, TasksBackend, ContactsBackend, FileNodeBackend, SharingBackend, MetadataBackend) all declare `supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool` without caller/account_id args. Their doc-comments explicitly promise per-account semantics ("Returns true if this account supports the given JMAP object type") but the signatures cannot honor that promise — they have no account_id in scope.

Root finding: JMAP-x2gd.46 (filed against chat-server). The defect is workspace-wide because jmap-mail-server is the canonical extension-server template per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" and every sibling mirrors its method shapes. Fixing this in chat-server alone would create canonical-template divergence; the sweep must be coordinated.

Scope:
- 8 backend.rs trait declarations (1 line each + doc-comment update)
- 8 memory.rs reference-impl signatures
- ~16 in-crate test-stub backends in lib.rs/event.rs/tests/common
- ~3 external test consumers (sharing-server query_changes_tests.rs, mail-server integration.rs, mail-server/chat-server tests/common/mod.rs)
- 8 PLAN.md / README.md doc strings that mention the old signature
- testjig wiring (jmap-testjig consumes all 8 backends)

Coordination order per chat-server AGENTS.md "🧬 Sibling of the canonical jmap-mail-server — mirror its shape":

1. Land canonical first: jmap-mail-server backend.rs + memory.rs + lib.rs test stubs + tests/common/mod.rs + tests/integration.rs.
2. Then propagate same-pass to: chat-server, calendars-server, tasks-server, contacts-server, filenode-server, sharing-server, metadata-server. Each crate gets backend.rs + memory.rs + (lib.rs|event.rs) + tests/common/mod.rs (if present) updated together.
3. Update jmap-testjig (consumes all 8) to compile against the new shape.
4. Update each crate's PLAN.md and README.md prose to match.
5. Run cargo check --workspace, cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc.

Backward-compat note: this is a public-API breaking signature change for every downstream consumer that implements a Backend trait. Default impl in trait declaration accepts the new args (`fn supports_type<O>(&self, _caller, _account_id) -> bool { true }`-style trivial default could be added in the same change). With a default impl, the breaking change becomes "consumer impls that previously matched the signature exactly now no longer match (signature differs by arity)". The override case is the breaking case — there are downstream consumers that override this method today, and they will fail to compile until they add the new args.

Default-impl proposal: keep default impl returning `true` (cheap default for the trivial case). Override case requires adding the two new params. Default-impl arity drift IS the breaking change; cannot be hidden via deprecated alias.

Decomposition: file 9 child beads — 1 per crate (8) + 1 for jmap-testjig wiring. Each child is independently mergeable on top of the canonical-first commit. The canonical (mail-server) is the first commit; the 8 propagation commits can follow in parallel.

Workspace-wide MSRV / SemVer impact: this needs a pre-1.0 minor bump on each crate. The kit is currently in the pre-publish phase per workspace.toml; the breaking change does NOT cross a published 1.0 boundary.

Sibling beads under the same family (deferred — these need similar architectural sign-off):
- JMAP-x2gd.43 (limits() is sync but per-account semantics promised by doc — limits() shape is the model THIS bead wants supports_type to copy; .43 is about a DIFFERENT angle on the same method, async-ness, and is opinion-coloured)
- JMAP-x2gd.47 (may_set_custom_emoji bool→reason loss — different gate hook, different issue)
- JMAP-x2gd.50 (5-method sync-vs-async pattern — supports_type is one of the 5, but generate_invite_code / protect_last_admin / retains_edit_history are also sync; this bead deals with the args, not the async-ness)

Recommend doing this BEFORE the kit publishes 1.0 to any of the 8 crates. Pre-publish is the cheapest moment to land a coordinated breaking signature change.
notes: DECIDED by Mark 2026-10-19: option 2. Signature becomes fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self, caller: &Self::CallerCtx, account_id: &jmap_types::Id) -> bool, required (no default), mirroring limits(). Preconditions confirmed: crates pre-1.0 (0.2.0 published, 0.3.0 already breaking); no out-of-tree overrides (kith, mimid, chinwag, stoa grep clean). Rationale: all call sites are handlers with caller/account_id in scope (mail snippet.rs:64, filenode.rs x6); RFC 8620 accountCapabilities and accountNotSupportedByMethod are per-account. Order: mail-server canonical, then 7 siblings, then testjig. Ships in 0.3.0 (breaking). Run after the P1 lane integration lands.
close_reason: Landed as 360cb1ce (mail canonical) + a47b6ebc (siblings): per-account required supports_type (Mark option 2). Review passed; CI green at 667a161f.
